text: The override the review forum reviews is the open deviation record of the case at DEV_WITH_OWNER: the review is the outcome-recording step of the deviation stage on rwb-deviation, it declares no override table, no override column, no override path and no second outcome set, and the forum sees each deviation with its code, its raise facts, its paused state and its named handler.
why: TSD S8 T3.1 gives S8 one table with DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the FSD S8 A2.17.3.2 field catalog lists the same deviation fields only; no source defines an override entity, a review table or a review path, and inventing one would add a record, a table and a migration no document owns while the legacy criteria only ask that overrides reach the forum with their reason and their outcome.
read: TSD S8 T3.0, T3.1 and T4; FSD S8 A2.17.2 and A2.17.3.2; legacy RWB-E7-008 Story and Acceptance criteria; context pack ownership rows (one table, one workflow); Template and Rules v1 R9
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7008-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 BR1, 11, 13 and 15; RWB-S8-E7008-CON sections 2, 7 AC1 and AC2, 8 BR5, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Business lead and the solution architect, before wave 4 starts
impact: The review runs on the existing one-table model with no migration, and a build that adds an override entity fails the contract review

text: The forum's reason is carried by the note of the DeviationOutcome request and recorded in the local decision record; the outcome is the published LOV-DEV-OUTCOME of RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED; and no reason property, field ID, list or column is declared, so the reason's name, field ID and value format carry the placeholder until the business lead confirms them. A repeat of the same review is matched on the deviation reference and the outcome because API-S8-002 declares no Idempotency-Key.
why: The legacy text asks for the reason and the outcome of each override, the FSD names no reason field, deviation has no reason column, and the only published request element of the operation is DeviationOutcome with outcome and note (API Specification v4; TSD S8 T-A.2). Adding a column or an enumeration would invent a business value, and dropping the reason would lose the legacy requirement.
read: API Specification v4 components DeviationOutcome and Deviation; TSD S8 T-A.2, T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S8 A2.17.2 and A2.17.3.2; legacy RWB-E7-008 AC1, AC2 and Data; Template and Rules v1 R9
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7008-APP sections 2, 4, 8 BR2 and BR10, 11, 13 and 15; RWB-S8-E7008-CON sections 7 AC2, 8 BR6 and BR8, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Business lead and the rwb-deviation tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: The reason is recorded on the ledger with the outcome and no column or migration is added; a later reference-data list can arrive as an additive change

text: The DEVIATION rule package is read from rwb-decision at its version in force on a class C consumed row with a fake, evaluated by this service's own evaluator inside the workflow activity, and recorded with the rule ID that fired; no Drools kit is embedded and RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are recorded as absent.
why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, the R3 default ruling gives the rule package registry to rwb-decision, and the S8 row of the connection matrix carries no P7 edge although the review cannot record a rule version without the package. Recording an invented rule ID or embedding the kit would either misattribute the deliverable or add a dependency the plan does not hold.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings, R5.4 class C, R5.5 DP-04; TSD S8 T0.3, T2 and T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-11 and R-DEV-22; context pack connection matrix row S8
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7008-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 8 BR6, 11, 12.2 and 13; RWB-S8-E7008-CON sections 2, 7 AC3, 8 BR4, 11 and 12.2

impact: The package version and the rule ID are recorded with each review, the absent kit and P7 rows are tracked, and a later rule row can arrive in the package as reference data

text: The review records the outcome and moves the deviation on the DEVIATION_RESOLVED rows only: R-DEV-09 for X1 and X7 to DEV_RESOLVED, R-DEV-10 for X2 and R-DEV-22 for an outcome that names no next step to DEV_REROUTE. The recorded outcome CASE_ENDED closes no case here, because R-DEV-11 reaches CASE_ENDED on INSURANCE_SETTLED and belongs to the X3 path; cleared_at, the contact stop, the timers, the clock resume of R-DEV-18 and the route reopen of R-DEV-19 are FEAT-DVH-06's and the route stories'.
why: TSD S8 T4 gives the four rows and their from and to states, FSD S8 A2.6 gives the clearance its own recorded outcome, the stop lift and the resume, and no source states that the review closes a case. Claiming the clearance here would duplicate FEAT-DVH-06 and would write the timers and the stop, which this service does not own as a review step.
read: TSD S8 T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-11, R-DEV-18, R-DEV-19 and R-DEV-22; FSD S8 A2.6 and A2.17.2; legacy RWB-E7-008 AC1
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7008-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 5 X6, 8 BR4 and BR9, 9, 11, 13 and 19; RWB-S8-E7008-CON sections 7 AC5 and AC7, 8 BR7 and BR14, 9 and 12.3

impact: The review ends at the recorded outcome and the rule-driven state, the clearance stories keep cleared_at and the clock, and a build that writes them fails the boundary test

text: The review publishes and consumes no event: the stage outcome of the deviation state and the outcome returns to the parent CaseWorkflow on task queue rwb-case over the parent-child workflow edge, EV-06 DeviationRaised and EV-07 DeviationCleared remain the raise and clearance steps', the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as a missing H row, and the deviation-list read of SCR-08 has no published operation and carries the placeholder.
why: The ownership rows give the service two REST operations and one workflow, the event catalogue gives it two events that carry a raise and a clear, and the matrix row S8 reaches P3 by Temporal and events. A review that lifts no stop and closes no case has no event to publish, and a list read declared without a source would invent an interface; the absence is tracked instead.
read: Context pack ownership rows (2 REST operations, EV-06 and EV-07, workflow DeviationWorkflow) and connection matrix row S8; Event and Messaging Design v4; TSD S8 T5.2, T5.3 and T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14

text: The review is authorised on the case-record right U of the published operation: RW-RISK, the primary role the FSD names, holds R in TSD S8 T6.1, as do RW-CONDUCT and RW-COE, so the matrix row is not widened, the conflict is recorded, and the roles that record or read a review are the twelve identities that hold U plus the four read-only roles the feature names.
why: FSD S8 A2.17.3.3 names the Risk and model risk officer as primary with the Conduct and QA officer and the Center of excellence analyst as also-uses, the legacy permission table gives the case record right U, and TSD S8 T-A.1 declares right U on both operations, while TSD S8 T6.1 gives all three R. Taking the matrix alone would leave the feature with no role that can record it, and granting a new right would invent an access row.
read: FSD S8 A2.17.3.3; TSD S8 T6.1 and T-A.1; legacy RWB-E7-008 Permission checks; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08

impact: The review is authorised for the twelve holders of U, the three read-only roles are named, and the matrix correction is tracked; no new role and no new right is introduced

text: The legacy permission table's 'and 4 more' holders of case-record right U are resolved to RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT, SY-CASEWF and SY-DATALOAD, the four further identities TSD S8 T6.1 gives U on that capability area besides the eight roles the legacy table names.
why: The legacy table names eight roles and says 'and 4 more' without listing them, and TSD S8 T6.1 gives U to exactly twelve identities: the eight named plus RW-DEBTSALE (RU), RW-GUARANT (RU), SY-CASEWF (CRU) and SY-DATALOAD (CU), with every other identity on R. The count and the matrix agree, so no further source is needed.

text: Wave 4 and release 31 May 2027 stay as the plan gives them for both stories: EP07 is wave 4 and the service's Arch v5 wave is 2, so the W-MAP wave is not earlier than the service wave and no conflict row is raised, and the release date is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
why: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 raises a conflict only where the W-MAP wave is earlier than the Arch v5 wave and keeps the W-MAP wave in that case; here EP07 is later, so the plan's wave stands with no conflict. U7 and R9 say a release date is copied unchanged, marked tentative and never raised as a gap.
